**MindWell Sleep Study Terms of Service Summary**

The service is called the "MindWell Sleep Study," a study examining the effects of a sleep-tracking app on insomnia.

Here are the key provisions:

* **Purpose:** The study focuses on using a sleep-tracking app to help with insomnia. (Clause 1)
* **Participation requirements:** Participants wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete weekly surveys. (Clause 2)
* **Risks:** The risk of skin irritation from the sensor strap is considered minimal. (Clause 3)
* **Data sharing:** De-identified data (data that is not linked to your personal name or contact information) can be shared with universities, but identifiable data will not be shared outside the research team. (Clause 4)
* **Withdrawal:** You can withdraw from the study at any time without facing any penalty. (Clause 5)
* **Payment:** Participants receive $75 once they complete the study. (Clause 6)
* **Contact information:** If you have questions, contact the IRB (Institutional Review Board) at irb@example.edu. (Clause 7)

**Clauses to be aware of:**

* **Data sharing (Clause 4):** If you're concerned about your personal data being shared, this clause says that identifiable data will not be shared outside the research team. However, if you're still concerned, you might want to ask questions about how identified data is handled.
* **Payment terms (Clause 6):** You'll only receive $75 if you complete the study. If you withdraw early, you won't get paid.
source_tos:
INFORMED CONSENT — MINDWELL SLEEP STUDY

1. PURPOSE. This study examines the effects of a sleep-tracking app on insomnia.
2. PROCEDURES. Participants wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete weekly surveys.
3. RISKS. Minimal risk: skin irritation from the sensor strap.
4. DATA. De-identified data may be shared with collaborating universities. Identifiable data will not be shared outside the research team.
5. WITHDRAWAL. You may withdraw at any time without penalty.
6. COMPENSATION. Participants receive $75 upon completion.
7. CONTACT. For questions contact the IRB at irb@example.edu.

- De-identified data may be shared with collaborators; identifiable data is kept within the research team.
- Withdrawal is allowed at any time without penalty.
- Compensation is $75 on completion.

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GOOGLE TERMS OF SERVICE (2020 → 2022) (Effective 2022; replaces the 2020 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Google and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2022 version differs from the 2020 version in the following ways: Reorganized the document into clearer sections, simplified language around what users can expect and what Google can do, and added more explicit content rules and warranty/liability disclaimers. Comparison: policies.google.com/terms/archive/20200331-20220105.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Google to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policies.google.com/terms/archive/20220105?hl=en-US . The previous version is available at https://policies.google.com/terms/archive/20200331?hl=en-US .

The Terms of Service outline the agreement between you and Microsoft for its various services and products. The service name is the "Microsoft Services Agreement."

Under these terms, Microsoft can update the agreement at any time, and you agree to be bound by these updates. 

Key provisions include:

* **Content and License**: When you submit content to Microsoft, you grant the company a license to use, operate, improve, and (if applicable) train its AI/ML systems. However, Microsoft will respect your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: Microsoft will follow its published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. 
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most of the services will resolve disputes through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)** with a 30-day opt-out window after opening an account for new users (some services, like Xbox, have specific requirements).

Flags to consider:
- **Auto-renewal for trial offers (clause not explicitly highlighted)**: 
  Some trial offers might require auto-renewal, so if you're not sure, be sure to review the terms carefully.

- **Termination of account**:
  Either party can terminate the agreement. Since the Terms of Service do not explicitly state what happens to your data when the account is terminated, it's possible that your content and data may be lost.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Added a new 'exportable data' subsection under Your Content, clarified that some services may have separate support terms, added language that some trial offers may require auto-renewal, and updated Xbox service-specific terms regarding sign-in to non-Microsoft platforms. Documented in Microsoft's Updates page (servicesagreement/Updates).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ . The previous version is available at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/upcoming.aspx .

The Terms of Service govern the relationship between Microsoft and its users, applying to products and services listed on the company's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all Microsoft services and products.
* **Content and License:** Microsoft can use user-submitted content to improve and train its AI and machine learning systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The company cross-references its published Privacy Policy, which explains how personal data is collected and processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Binding arbitration is required, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means that disputes are resolved through a private process instead of court (binding arbitration).
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions in the live document.
* **Contact:** Users can find answers to their questions about these terms and contact Microsoft's legal department at the provided URL.

**Harmful Clauses to Flag:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** While arbitration may be faster and less expensive than court proceedings, it can limit users' access to a fair and public trial (binding arbitration).
* **Termination:** The terms allow Microsoft to terminate the agreement, potentially restricting users' access to the services.

**Additional Information:**

* The updated terms now include clarifications on moderation and enforcement, and expanded language addressing third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data.
* User data is subject to the company's Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* Users should carefully review the terms and the Privacy Policy before using Microsoft services, particularly regarding data usage and dispute resolution.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (2023 → 2024) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added clarifications around moderation/enforcement with a link to external policy pages, expanded Xbox section to address third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data, and updated the kids-on-Xbox subsection regarding family settings on third-party platforms.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/Updates . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023*/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ .

- Key change: Added clarifications around moderation/enforcement with a link to external policy pages, expanded Xbox section to address third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data, and updated the kids-on-Xbox subsection regarding family settings on third-party platforms.

**OpenAI Terms of Use (Consumer)**

These Terms of Service outline the relationship between you and OpenAI, governing our interactions through our products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

*   **Scope**: These Terms apply to all OpenAI products and services you use, as described on our official terms page.
*   **Content and License**: We use your submitted content to improve our AI/ML systems, following your settings and applicable law.
*   **Privacy**: Our Privacy Policy (available on our website) explains what personal data we collect and how we process it.
*   **Dispute Resolution**: Most terms require **binding arbitration**, which means you waive the right to a jury trial and class-action lawsuits. However, you have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
*   **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under specific conditions.
*   **Contact**: For questions about these terms, visit our published legal contact information at [https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/](https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/).

**Harmful Clauses to Consider:**

*   **Binding Arbitration**: This requires you to take disputes to a private process instead of a public court. While you can opt out within 30 days of creating your account, consider the implications of waiving your right to a jury trial.
*   **Class-Action Waiver**: This means you can't participate in group lawsuits, potentially limiting your ability to address widespread issues or seek compensation.

These terms aim to provide a clear understanding of your relationship with OpenAI. If you have specific questions or concerns, please contact us as indicated.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI TERMS OF USE (CONSUMER) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Split the consumer Terms of Use from a separate Business Terms (for API/Enterprise) effective January 31, 2024, switched arbitration provider from ADR Services to National Arbitration and Mediation, and revised the dispute-resolution and batch-arbitration procedures. Documented at help.openai.com/en/articles/8541945.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use .

**OpenAI Services Agreement (Business/API)**

The Terms of Service govern your relationship with OpenAI and apply to various business services, including AI/ML products and APIs.

**Key Provisions:**

- **Scope**: These terms govern all products and services provided by OpenAI, listed on their official terms page.
- **Content and License**: When you use OpenAI services, your content is used to improve and train their AI/ML systems. You can control how your content is used through your settings.
- **Privacy**: OpenAI will collect personal data as described in their Privacy Policy.
- **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be settled through binding arbitration, which means a private dispute process instead of going to court. This applies unless you opt-out within 30 days of creating a new account (this exception is limited to services like Steam).
- **Termination**: You can terminate the agreement at any time, but you must follow the conditions outlined in the Terms of Service.

**Clauses of Note:**

- **Binding Arbitration**: This clause might be considered **harmful** as it limits your options for resolving disputes and may result in reduced compensation.
- **Class-Action Waivers**: As part of the binding arbitration clause, class-action waivers restrict users from joining or participating in group lawsuits.
- **No Opt-Out for Existing Accounts**: Unfortunately, this benefit is only applicable to new account holders with a 30-day window to opt-out of binding arbitration. Existing account holders may be required to use binding arbitration for dispute resolution.

**Additional Notes:**

- The company's published Privacy Policy outlines how personal data is processed.
- The Terms of Service and any disputes related to it can be found on the company's published legal contact information.

These Terms of Service primarily focus on governing interactions between you and OpenAI as you utilize their business services, and the service description is concise with an emphasis on highlighting key provisions and a note on the potentially limiting effect of the binding arbitration clause.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI SERVICES AGREEMENT (BUSINESS/API) (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Replaced the prior Business Terms with a single OpenAI Services Agreement effective May 31, 2025, covering API, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Team and other business services, with updated provisions on data handling, indemnification and SLAs. Announcement: community.openai.com/t/new-openai-services-agreement-effective-may-31-2025/1249405.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://openai.com/policies/business-terms/ .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC CONSUMER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Updated effective October 8, 2025: clarified scope (Claude.ai, Claude Pro, Claude apps), added explicit Acceptable Use Policy reference, refined provisions on business/enterprise email-domain linking, and updated dispute-resolution and governing-law sections. Versioning tracked at tostracker.app/document/anthropic.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms .

source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC COMMERCIAL TERMS OF SERVICE (API) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added more detailed sections on customer data and outputs, clarified that customer prompts and completions are not used to train models by default, and updated indemnification and acceptable-use language tied to the published Usage Policy.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms .

**Service Name:** Meta (Facebook) Terms of Service

These terms govern your relationship with Meta (Facebook) when using their products and services, which are listed on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Using Meta's products means you agree to these terms**: By using Meta's services, you're automatically agreeing to the terms and conditions outlined here.
* **What happens to your content**: Meta uses your uploaded content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, as specified in your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is collected and processed under Meta's published **Privacy Policy** (not outlined in these terms).
* **Dispute Resolution**: In case of disputes, most of the terms require **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of going to court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the live document.
* **Contact**: For questions about these terms, see Meta's legal contact information at the listed URL.

**Harmful Clauses to Note:**

* **Binding arbitration**: While this process can be faster and cheaper, it can also limit your ability to seek redress in a public court.
* **Class-action waivers**: These prevent users from joining a class action lawsuit against Meta.
* **Termination**: While either party can terminate the agreement, the terms don't provide clear conditions for how Meta will notify users or what happens to user data after termination.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FACEBOOK / META TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Facebook) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 1, 2025: tightened opening agreement language ('using these products means you agree'), added clearer license framing for content uploaded to Meta Products, and added wording about Meta's use of AI/machine-learning systems on user content for service improvement and safety.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Facebook) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.facebook.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.facebook.com/terms .

The service name is Instagram Terms of Use.

Here's a plain-language summary of these Terms of Service:

**Who they cover**: These Terms of Service cover your relationship with Meta (the company behind Instagram) and apply to Instagram and its services.

**Key provisions**:

* **Content sharing**: When you post on Instagram, you give Meta a non-exclusive license to use, distribute, and modify your content. This includes using your content to train their artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems.
* **Data collection**: Meta can collect your data as described in their Privacy Policy. The Privacy Policy explains how your personal data is used and processed.
* **Arbitration**: In case of a dispute, both you and Meta agree to use private arbitration (binding arbitration) instead of going to court. This means that if you sue Meta or they sue you, you'll have to resolve the issue through a private mediation process, rather than in a public court. There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either you or Meta can terminate the agreement at any time, subject to the conditions described in the terms.

**Harmful clauses to flag**:

* **Mandatory arbitration**: As mentioned earlier, arbitration can be useful for resolving disputes quickly, but it may limit your ability to speak publicly about the issue. Also, it's worth noting that you have a 30-day opt-out window when creating a new account, so you can choose not to agree to this provision initially.
* **Class-action waivers**: If you agree to arbitration, you may also waive your right to participate in class-action lawsuits (lawsuits with multiple plaintiffs who have similar claims).

Keep in mind that these Terms of Service are subject to change, and you should review them regularly for any updates. If you have questions or concerns, you can contact Meta through their published legal contact information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — INSTAGRAM TERMS OF USE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Instagram) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Aligned with the Meta umbrella update effective January 1, 2025: explicit grant of a worldwide non-exclusive license to use, distribute and modify uploaded content, and new wording referencing AI features and data processing across Meta Products.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Instagram) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 .

Please review these Terms of Service carefully if you're concerned about any of these points.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — X TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with X (Twitter) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective November 15, 2024: added an explicit, royalty-free, worldwide license for X to use posted content for training machine-learning and generative-AI models, removed the prior in-product opt-out language, and broadened third-party data-sharing permissions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by X (Twitter) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://x.com/en/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240515000000*/https://twitter.com/en/tos .

**Service Name:** TikTok Terms of Service (US)

The Terms of Service outline the rules and expectations between you (the user) and TikTok (the company). Here's a summary:

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope:** These terms govern your relationship with TikTok and apply to all products and services listed on their official terms page.
2. **Content and License:** When you upload content to TikTok, you give the company a license to use it to improve and train their AI/ML systems (if you allow it). The company will display your content 'as is', with some rules around generative-AI output (more on that below).
3. **Privacy:** The terms reference TikTok's separate Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed.
4. **Dispute Resolution:** In case of a dispute, you'll likely have to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a class-action waiver. You have a 30-day window to opt out, but note that this provision may not apply to all users (e.g., those from Steam/Valve).
5. **Termination:** Either you or TikTok can end the agreement under specific conditions (as outlined in the live document).

**Clauses to Flag:**

* **Generative-AI rules:** While the terms prohibit output stripping or claiming AI output as human-made, this provision might be a reminder to double-check where AI-generated content originates.
* **Binding arbitration:** As mentioned, this can be a limiting factor, especially if you have a group complaint or individual issue that might benefit from a more public, court-led resolution.
* **Sublicensable license:** This means TikTok can use your content without needing direct permission from you, as long as it's for training their AI/ML systems.

Remember to review the Privacy Policy and other related documents for a more detailed understanding of how TikTok handles your personal data and content.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TIKTOK TERMS OF SERVICE (US) (Effective 2026; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with TikTok and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective January 22, 2026: contracting party changed to TikTok USDS following the US joint venture; added explicit generative-AI rules (output 'as is', user responsibility for inputs/outputs, prohibition on stripping watermarks or claiming AI output is human-made); reaffirmed sublicensable license to use content for training ML models.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by TikTok to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en .

**Service Name:** YouTube (the service is governed by a set of updated Terms of Service, which became effective in 2021).

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to YouTube's products and services.
* **Content and License:** When you upload content to YouTube, you grant the company the right to use and share your content for various purposes, such as improving AI/ML systems (artificial intelligence and machine learning). However, this use is subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Monetization:** YouTube now has the right to monetize most uploaded videos, even if you're not a Partner creator (previously, only Partner creators could monetize their content).
* **Facial Recognition:** The company prohibits the collection of facial recognition data from videos.
* **US Tax Withholding:** If you're a non-US creator, YouTube updated your US tax withholding obligations.
* **Privacy:** The terms reference YouTube's published Privacy Policy, which explains how it collects and processes personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with class-action waivers. You have 30 days to opt-out if you're a new account holder.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Monetization:** As mentioned, YouTube can now monetize most uploaded videos without your explicit permission. You may not receive compensation for your content, even if it brings value to YouTube.
* **Binding Arbitration:** The requirement for binding arbitration means you may have limited options for resolving disputes with YouTube. A class-action waiver also restricts your ability to join a group lawsuit against the company.
* **Privacy:** Although the terms cross-reference the Privacy Policy, the policy itself may not be fully transparent. Understand how YouTube collects and uses your personal data.

**Notable Exceptions:** The Steam (Valve) is not included in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024.

Please note that this summary only covers the changes and updates since 2019 and is based on the provided information. For a comprehensive understanding of the Terms of Service, you should review the full document.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — YOUTUBE TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2021; replaces the 2019 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with YouTube and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2021 version differs from the 2019 version in the following ways: Effective June 1, 2021 globally: introduced YouTube's right to monetize most videos (including non-Partner videos), banned collection of facial-recognition data from videos, and updated US tax-withholding obligations for non-US creators. Summary at support.google.com/youtube/answer/10090902.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by YouTube to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.youtube.com/static?template=terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20191101000000*/https://www.youtube.com/static?template=terms .

**Adobe General Terms of Use Summary**

These terms govern your relationship with Adobe, the company behind popular products like Photoshop and Illustrator. The key provisions are outlined below:

* **Scope**: These terms apply to Adobe's products and services listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content (e.g., images, text), Adobe uses it to operate, improve, and (if applicable) train AI/ML systems, in line with your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Adobe's published Privacy Policy describes what personal data is collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most updates require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. Note: Steam is an exception, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024.
* **Termination**: Either party can end the agreement under conditions outlined in the live document.
* **Contact**: For questions, visit Adobe's published legal contact information at [https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html](https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html).

Some users may find certain clauses potentially concerning:

- Adobe can **access user content** via automated and manual methods to improve services and software. While this should improve the user experience, it raises questions about data collection and usage.
- There is no explicit **opt-out for AI model training** on user-submitted cloud content. However, the current version of the terms states Adobe does not train generative AI models on such content.
- **Binding arbitration** (a private dispute resolution process) may limit users' access to a court and potentially result in an unfair outcome.

Keep in mind that Adobe has added clearer language to their terms, and users can find information about recent changes and updates at [https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html](https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html). If you're unsure about any specific provision, consider visiting the contact page for more information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ADOBE GENERAL TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Adobe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: February 2024 update added language allowing Adobe to access user content via 'automated and manual methods' to improve services and software. After backlash in June 2024, Adobe rewrote sections in clearer language, explicitly stating it does not train generative-AI models on customer cloud content and added a plain-English summary of changes.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Adobe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html .

**Service Name:** Zoom Terms of Service, effective 2023.

**Summary:**

These Terms of Service cover the relationship between you (the user) and Zoom. Key provisions include how Zoom uses your data and content, how you can interact with the service, and what happens in case of disputes.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to all Zoom products and services listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Zoom uses your submitted content (e.g., audio, video, messages) to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Zoom cross-references their published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will go to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window when creating a new account.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
* **Contact**: For questions, see Zoom's published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **AI/ML model training**: While Zoom says they won't use your content to train AI models without consent, the 2023 update permits using 'Service Generated Data' for this purpose. This may concern users who are not comfortable with their data being used for AI training.

It's essential to be aware of these terms and make informed decisions about using the Zoom service. If you have concerns or questions, review Zoom's Privacy Policy and published legal contact information for more information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ZOOM TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Zoom and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: March 2023 update added broad license over 'Service Generated Data' permitting use to train AI/ML models. Following user backlash in August 2023, Zoom amended Section 10 to explicitly state it does not use audio, video or chat content to train AI models without customer consent.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Zoom to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.zoom.com/en/trust/terms/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230301000000*/https://explore.zoom.us/en/terms/ .

**Service Name: LinkedIn User Agreement**

These are the rules that govern your relationship with LinkedIn and its services.

**Key Provisions:**

• **Scope**: These terms apply to all LinkedIn products and services listed on their official terms page.
• **Content and License**: When you share content on LinkedIn, they might use it to improve their services, including artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
• **Privacy**: The terms reference LinkedIn's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed.
• **Dispute Resolution**: You must use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) to resolve disagreements, with some exceptions. You can opt out of this requirement within 30 days of creating a new account.
• **Termination**: Either party can end the agreement under specific conditions outlined in the document.
• **Contact**: For questions about these terms, check LinkedIn's published legal contact information.

**Potential Issues to Consider:**

* Class-action waivers in dispute resolution (binding arbitration) may limit your right to group claims and proceed in court as a collective.
* Although you can opt out of arbitration, this might be a concern if you have a legitimate grievance against LinkedIn.
* The use of your content to train AI/ML systems may be problematic, although the terms mention an opt-out toggle in Settings.

Please note that these concerns are based on a plain-language interpretation and might not be exhaustive.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — LINKEDIN USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with LinkedIn and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: November 20, 2024 update added explicit references to use of member data and content to train generative AI models for LinkedIn features (with an opt-out toggle in Settings). Also updated dispute-resolution and class-action waiver provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by LinkedIn to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement . The previous version is available at https://www.linkedin.com/legal/previous-user-agreement .

**Slack User Terms of Service Summary**

The document we'll be discussing governs your relationship with Slack, a communication platform for teams. The terms apply to the services and products listed on Slack's official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Use of User Content:** Slack uses your content (e.g., messages, files) to improve, operate, and train its AI and Machine Learning (ML) systems, subject to your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** The terms refer you to Slack's **published Privacy Policy**, which outlines the types of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If there's a dispute, both parties must use **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**, with a **30-day opt-out window for new accounts**. This means you can choose not to use arbitration when you first sign up, but it's not a one-time choice – for subsequent disputes, you'll need to opt-in again.
* **Termination:** Either Slack or you can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions listed in the terms.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about these terms, you can find contact information in the live document.

**Potentially Harmful Clauses:**

* **Binding Arbitration:** This can make it difficult to resolve disputes through the courts. Opting out within the 30-day window helps, but you should review this carefully.
* **Termination:** Be sure you understand the conditions for terminating the agreement, as this might affect your access to Slack services.

**Important Reminders:**

* Make sure to check the published Privacy Policy for detailed information on data collection and processing.
* Review and opt out of binding arbitration if you'd prefer to resolve disputes in court.

The Terms of Service offer a comprehensive framework for your relationship with Slack. Take some time to review the key provisions and understand your rights and responsibilities.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SLACK USER TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Slack and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Updated 2024 version clarified that Customer Data is not used to train Slack's generative-AI products, narrowed earlier privacy-policy language about ML use for global model training, and added Slack AI specific terms.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Slack to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.

The service is called the GitHub Terms of Service. These Terms of Service explain your relationship with GitHub and the products and services they offer.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These Terms apply to all products and services described on GitHub's official terms page.
* **Personal Data**: GitHub may collect, use, and share personal data with its affiliates (such as Microsoft) for artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) model development, product development, and user preference matching.
* **Content and License**: GitHub uses your submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Binding Arbitration**: If there's a dispute, you agree to resolve it through binding arbitration, which means you waive your right to a class-action lawsuit and will use a private dispute resolution process instead of going to court.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.

**Flags:**

* **Data Sharing**: You may have concerns about how your personal data is shared with GitHub's affiliates. The Terms allow them to share your data with other affiliates, including Microsoft, for AI/ML model development and product development.
* **Arbitration**: You should be aware that the Terms require binding arbitration, which means you waive your right to a class-action lawsuit and may be required to participate in a private dispute resolution process.
* **No Transparency**: The Terms do not provide clear guidance on how your personal data is processed or how AI/ML systems are trained. You may need to review GitHub's published Privacy Policy separately to understand the details.

Keep in mind that these Terms reflect a complex agreement between user and service provider. Users should take the time to review the document in full for further information and clarification.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GITHUB TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2026; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with GitHub and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: March 2026 update expanded the Affiliates section so personal data may be shared with Microsoft and other GitHub affiliates for AI/ML model development, added a new product-development purpose for using personal data to train AI features, and clarified that user opt-out preferences propagate to affiliates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by GitHub to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service .

The Terms of Service for Reddit's User Agreement applies to their products and services (listed on their official terms page).

Here are the key provisions:

* **Content and License**: When you post content on Reddit, you grant the company a license to use it in various ways, such as operating, improving, or training AI/ML systems (subject to your settings and applicable law).
* **Privacy**: The terms refer to Reddit's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. Note that Steam (Valve) is an exception.
* **Termination**: Either party may end the agreement with certain conditions, as outlined in the current document.

Some clauses to be mindful of:

* **User content licensing**: By using Reddit, you grant permission for your content to potentially be used by third parties, including for AI training. This may not align with your expectations.
* **Binding arbitration**: This means that disputes will be resolved privately, rather than through a public court process.

It's essential to review these terms and Reddit's associated policies before using their services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — REDDIT USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2023; replaces the 2021 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Reddit and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2021 version in the following ways: September 2023 update added explicit terms confirming Reddit's right to license user content to third parties (including for AI training), added new monetization-related provisions and shifted dispute-resolution venue. Reddit publishes prior versions at redditinc.com/policies.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Reddit to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.redditinc.com/policies/user-agreement . The previous version is available at https://www.redditinc.com/policies/user-agreement-september-12-2021 .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

The service is called Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions. To summarize, the Terms of Service outline Apple's rules for using their digital media services, which include products like Apple Music, iCloud, and the App Store.

Here are the key provisions:

**Scope**: These terms apply to your relationship with Apple and control how you use their services.

**Content and License**: Apple can use your submitted content, like data or media, to improve their AI/ML systems, but only if you've allowed it in your settings or if it's required by the law.

**Privacy**: Apple's Privacy Policy explains how they collect and process your personal data, but you should read that policy specifically for details.

**Dispute Resolution**: If a dispute arises, Apple wants to resolve it through private arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. However, Steam (Valve) is not required to use this method. Note that class-action lawsuits are not an option in these arbitration proceedings.

One potential concern is the dispute resolution clause, which may limit your ability to take action in court or join a class-action lawsuit if you have a problem with Apple.

Here are the other key provisions:

- You can terminate the agreement, but the Terms and Conditions require specific conditions.
- Apple can also terminate the agreement under certain conditions.
- If you have questions about these Terms of Service, you can contact Apple through their published contact information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

The service name is iCloud. Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

**Overview**

These terms govern your relationship with Apple and outline the rules for using their iCloud services.

**Key Provisions**

* **Content Use**: When you upload content to iCloud, Apple may use it to improve their products, services, or AI/ML systems, but will follow your settings and applicable law.
* **Data Sharing**: Your content may be accessed by Apple if necessary for legal or safety reasons.
* **Arbitration**: If a dispute arises, you'll need to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers, unless you opt out within 30 days of creating your account.
* **Termination**: Either you or Apple can end the agreement at any time, but you should review the live document for terms.
* **Contact**: For questions, see Apple's published contact information.

**Harmful Clauses Flagged**

* While not explicitly stated, there's no clear guarantee about user data protection, raising concerns about data handling and storage practices.
* The binding arbitration provision may limit users' ability to seek redress in court, potentially making disputes more difficult to resolve.
* The clause allowing Apple to access users' content for legal or safety reasons doesn't provide specific information about what these reasons entail, which may raise data protection concerns.

**Other Concerns**

* There's a notice about the 30-day opt-out window for arbitration, but no clear instructions on how to do so.
* Previous versions of the Terms of Service are not available, making it difficult to assess changes and any implications for users who continued to use the service.

Keep in mind that these are the main concerns and inferences drawn from the provided text. Users should consider their individual circumstances and concerns when using the service.

Note that this is not a legal analysis but rather a summary of the terms provided.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ICLOUD TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Advanced Data Protection (end-to-end encryption) language, references to Apple Intelligence Private Cloud Compute, and revised provisions about how stored content may be accessed by Apple for legal/safety reasons.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20220101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html .

**Service Name:** Canva Terms of Use (TOS)

**Key Provisions:**

* The Canva TOS is a binding agreement between you (the user) and Canva, governing your use of their products and services.
* Canva reserves the right to change or terminate the service at any time, subject to certain conditions.
* **Generated Content:** If you use Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio), you own the output, but Canva retains certain platform rights and restrictions apply to using such content to train other AI models. Be aware that you're subject to new content-moderation and labeling requirements.
* **Content and License:** Canva uses your submitted content to operate and improve their AI/ML systems, following your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The TOS references Canva's published Privacy Policy, explaining what personal data is collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You agree to binding arbitration, which is a private dispute process instead of court (although you can opt-out within 30 days of creating a new account). This means you won't have access to a traditional court system.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to conditions in the live document.

**Potential Concerns:**

* The use of binding arbitration may limit your access to a traditional court system and the ability to participate in class-action suits.
* The terms for generated content may restrict how you use AI-generated content, raising questions about ownership and control.
* The TOS does not explicitly provide for a clear way to resolve disputes outside of arbitration.

**Where to Seek Help:**

If you have questions or concerns about the Canva TOS, refer to the company's published legal contact information at the Canva website.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — CANVA TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Canva and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added rules for Canva's generative AI tools (Magic Studio): users own outputs subject to platform rights, restrictions on using Canva-generated content to train other AI models, and new content-moderation/labeling requirements.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Canva to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.canva.com/policies/terms-of-use/ .

**Service Name:** The 23andMe Terms of Service

The 23andMe Terms of Service outline the agreement between you and the company when using their products and services. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope:** These terms apply to the products and services listed on the official 23andMe terms page.

**Usage of User Content:** 23andMe uses user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, but only according to your settings and applicable law.

**Privacy:** The terms reference 23andMe's published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data they collect and how it's processed.

**Dispute Resolution:** Most users will be required to resolve disputes through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), which has a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. However, users who don't take action within this window will be bound by this agreement.

**Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement according to the live document.

**Notes on Harmful Clauses:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration:** 23andMe requires users to resolve disputes through binding arbitration, which can limit users' ability to take their case to court. If you don't opt out within 30 days of creating an account, you'll be bound by this agreement.
* **Class-Action Waiver:** The terms also limit users' right to participate in class-action lawsuits.
* **Shortened Dispute-Notice Window:** The dispute-notice window was shortened, which may make it more difficult for users to resolve issues.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

**Roblox Terms of Use**

Roblox Terms of Service (TOS) govern your relationship with the platform. The latest version (2024) applies to various Roblox products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

### What They Mean

* **Content and License**: You retain ownership of your submitted content, but Roblox gets permission to use it for their AI/ML systems (if you've allowed it).
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is processed according to the Privacy Policy. We don't disclose more information about data collection here.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes go through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). There's a 30-day option to opt out for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can cancel the agreement with conditions described in the live document (which we can't see here).

### Flagged Clauses

* **Dispute Resolution**: Binding arbitration with a class-action waiver might restrict your right to join group lawsuits.
* **Termination**: Conditions are not specified here, but it may be concerning if you're uncertain about what led to termination.

### Important URLs

If you need help or have questions, see the help documentation at [https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us).

### Notable Exceptions

Steam (Valve) has removed mandatory arbitration in their platform; Roblox's policy differs from theirs on this point.

The Terms of Service do not address concerns unrelated to these provisions.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ROBLOX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Roblox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.

**Service Name:** Uber US Terms of Use

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope:** These terms apply to Uber's products and services as described on the official terms page.
2. **Content License:** Uber uses user-submitted content to improve and train its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. (This means Uber can use information you provide to improve its services, but only in ways you've agreed to.)
3. **Privacy:** Uber's published Privacy Policy explains how personal data is collected and processed. (You can find the full policy by contacting the company.)
4. **Dispute Resolution:** You agree to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a class-action waiver. However, there's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. (This means you'll likely resolve disputes outside of court, without joining a class action lawsuit.)
5. **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement with notice.
6. **Contact:** For questions, see the company's published contact information.

**Harmful Clauses to Note:**

* **Dispute Resolution:** The requirement for binding arbitration with a class-action waiver may limit your ability to take part in class action lawsuits, which can be beneficial for collective action.
* **Content License:** While Uber can use user-submitted content for improvement, it's unclear how this affects data protection or potential biases in AI algorithms.
* **Termination:** Without stating specific grounds, either party can terminate the agreement, which might leave users without notice or recourse.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — UBER US TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Uber and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update revised arbitration after the New Jersey Uber Eats arbitration decision, added language on AI-generated trip summaries and driver/rider safety features, and expanded liability sections regarding third-party services.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Uber to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.uber.com/legal/en/document/?country=united-states&lang=en&name=general-terms-of-use .
